# Compulsory Implantation While involuntary implantation is illegal in most cases, it can be authorized in a select few cases. Such authorization requires the filling of a form detailing the legal justification for said procedure, and must have the signatures and stamps (if applicable) of both the ordering authorities and the medical professional who will be performing the procedure. The two [italic]can[/italic] be the same person.
All such procedures must be performed by a medical professional, either a member of [lightblue]Medical[/lightblue], or the [red]Brigmedic[/red]. If the individual in question is unfit for implantation, either due to health risks or other complications, then the medical professional is obligated to refuse performing the procedure. ## Removal of Illegal Implants
Requires authorization by: [bold][red]Warden[/red][/bold] or [bold][red]Head of Security[/red][/bold]
Unauthorized implants of a contraband category of 3 or above can be removed and confiscated. Security is not obligated to replace missing limbs.
This procedure requires the individual to already be sentenced and in the brig. Removal of the implant counts as brig time, but is allowed to exceed their allotted sentence if needed. ## Compulsory Mindshielding
Compulsory mindshielding can be done for two reasons: ### Removal of Mind Control
Requires authorization by: [bold][lightblue]Psychologist[/lightblue][/bold] OR [bold][lightblue]Chief Medical Officer[/lightblue][/bold], and the [bold][navy]Head of Security[/navy][/bold]
Persons believed to be under the effects of involuntary mind-control may be subjected to compulsory mindshielding to undo said mind-control. This requires a psychological evaluation to be performed on the individual, unless an Induced Mutiny is known to be afoot.
If the mind-shielding results in short-term memory loss, this is confirmation of [textlink="Induced Mutiny" link=InducedMutiny]. ### Testing Purposes
Requires authorization by: [bold][red]Head of Security[/red][/bold] and the [bold][navy]Captain[/navy][/bold] OR [bold][navy]Magistrate[/navy][/bold]
Persons believed to be guilty of Violations of Bodily Autonomy can be subjected to compulsory mindshielding to ascertain whether or not a nefarious organization sent them. This requires evidence of said violations of bodily autonomy, such as large stashes of suspect equipment, or at least two eye-witnesses having witnessed an incident involving the alleged implant.
If the mind-shielding fails, this is confirmation of [textlink="Induced Mutiny" link=InducedMutiny], and the subject is themselves automatically assumed guilty of Violations of Bodily Autonomy, as well as Refusal of Mental Shielding. The recommended sentence for this, is death. ## Compulsory Tracking
Requires authorization by: [bold][red]Warden[/red][/bold] or [bold][red]Head of Security[/red][/bold]
Persons who have been imprisoned more than two times, may be subjected to mandatory tracking on their third visit to the brig. The paperwork need only state the time and causes for their three incarcerations to be valid. ## Explorative Surgery
Requires authorization by: [bold][red]Head of Security[/red][/bold] and either a [bold][lightblue]Surgeon[/lightblue][/bold] or the [bold][lightblue]Chief Medical Officer[/lightblue][/bold]
Persons believed to be hiding illegal implants outside of immediate view can be subjected to explorative surgery, either via traditional surgery, or via an implant removal device.
Such procedures are only to be done if:
- At least two eye-witnesses witnessed the usage of such an implant. - An implantation device, or other relevant evidence, is found with DNA or fingerprints from the accused. - The accused has admitted themselves to the existence of their implants.
The procedure is only to proceed to the extent necessary to remove and/or prove the existence of whatever implant there is evidence of. Further exploration will require further evidence.
